payload.title: Scope spans and location kinds on detections
payload.description:
Give every detection a real scope span and an explicit location kind. Decision 3 of the parent initiative.

## Problem

In an internal dogfood scan, every component location was one line long. The pattern engine sets `endLine` to `startLine` (`src/patterns/engine.ts`, `src/patterns/detectors/helpers.ts`). Import-triggered detectors record line 1 with no code (about a third of locations). Tightest-span matching cannot work on these.

## Scope

- Keep the matched line as the detection anchor.
- Add the enclosing function or class range from the analysis engine as the detection's scope span.
- Add a location kind: `import`, `call`, `declaration`, `file_membership`. Replace the line-1-with-no-code convention.
- Carry both through the canonical scan result, the OCSF projection, and `dataparade.json`.
- Confirm component stable ids do not change (they key on file paths, `src/core/pipeline/stable-component-ids.ts`).

## Done when

- `axios.post(` inside `sendWelcome()` produces a detection with the anchor line, a scope span equal to `sendWelcome`, and kind `call`.
- An SDK import produces kind `import` with no scope span and no line-1 placeholder.
- Tightest-span lookup over components returns the enclosing scope for a declaration inside it.

## Evaluation

- Components layer: matching stays on the anchor line. Scope extent is scored as a separate asserted attribute (does the reported scope contain the labeled declaration), only over gold that asserts it.
- Guard: a wider span must not raise component match rates on existing gold.
